QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_13

question.text: Which personal-trading policy control is MOST directly aimed at preventing 'front-running' by Investment Manager employees at a Cat III AIF?

answer.text: Mandatory pre-clearance of employee personal trades and blackout windows around the fund's trading orders
Annual trustee performance review of the AMC

explanation.text: The Logic: Front-running is where an employee trades ahead of the fund's known orders for personal benefit. The Code of Conduct for employees requires compliance pre-clearance of personal trades plus a trading-window closure (e.g., fresh pre-clearance is needed after 7 trading days) around the fund's own trades in the same security. These controls directly target front-running. The Trap: The other options are legitimate governance items but don't directly address front-running, which requires person-level trading surveillance and pre-clearance. Note: Pages 433-435 of the workbook describe the employee trading Code of Conduct, the trading-window closure, the compliance pre-clearance requirement, and the fresh pre-clearance after 7 trading days.
